title: Before You Get Married… Read This Before You Promise Forever
paragraphs:
Before You Get Married… Read This Before You Promise Forever
The Wedding Lasts a Day. The Covenant Shapes Eternity. Don't Prepare for a Ceremony While Neglecting Your Soul.
But almost nobody tells you to prepare for the marriage itself.
We spend months planning one beautiful day while neglecting the lifelong covenant that begins after the guests go home.
That may be one of the greatest tragedies of our generation.
Many people are searching for "the one."
Scripture tells us to become someone who belongs completely to the One who never leaves.
Marriage was never designed to complete you.
That truth alone has the power to save countless hearts from unnecessary heartbreak.
If your identity depends on another imperfect sinner, your foundation will eventually crack.
But if your identity rests in Christ, your marriage stands upon a Rock that storms cannot destroy.
"Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock." (Matthew 7:24)
He did not promise there would be no storms.
He promised the foundation would survive them.
That principle applies to marriage just as much as it applies to every other part of life.
The first wedding in history did not begin with romance.
"Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh." (Genesis 2:24)
The Hebrew expression דָּבַק (dāḇaq) means "to cling," "to hold fast," "to stick firmly."
Marriage was never intended to be disposable.
"Will you both help one another become holy?"
The Apostle Paul reveals one of marriage's deepest mysteries:
"This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church." (Ephesians 5:32)
Marriage is not merely about two people.
It is a living picture of the Gospel.
Every act of forgiveness reflects Christ.
Every moment of undeserved grace reflects Christ.
Every restoration points back to the Cross.
Marriage was always meant to preach Jesus without saying a word.
Before asking whether someone is attractive...
Before asking whether they are successful...
Ask whether they are submitted to Christ.
Before asking whether they make your heart race...
Ask whether they help your soul grow.
But a heart surrendered to Christ grows more beautiful with every passing year.
The Hebrew word חֶסֶד (ḥesed) is often translated "steadfast love," "covenant love," or "lovingkindness."
There is no perfect English equivalent because it carries the idea of loyal, faithful, covenant mercy that refuses to abandon.
That is how God loves His people.
Marriage becomes strongest when husbands and wives learn to love with that same covenant faithfulness.
Not because the other deserves it every day.
Because Christ loved us when we deserved judgment.
"God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us." (Romans 5:8)
Grace came before we deserved it.
And healthy marriages breathe that same air every day.
The Greek word Paul uses for love in 1 Corinthians 13 is ἀγάπη (agápē).
It is not primarily emotional attraction.
"Love is patient and kind... it does not insist on its own way... it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never ends." (1 Corinthians 13:4–8)
Imagine how different marriages would become if couples memorized this passage before memorizing wedding vows.
"How do I know if this is God's will?"
"Are we becoming more like Christ together?"
Because two people can share chemistry and still destroy one another spiritually.
Spiritual compatibility is not merely attending church together.
Keeping Christ at the center when emotions fail.
"Can two walk together, unless they have agreed to meet?" (Amos 3:3)
Can we admit when we're wrong?
Can we pray even after arguments?
Can we submit our opinions to Scripture?
Can we choose humility over pride?
Pressure exposes what comfort often hides.
Many people enter marriage believing love will erase selfishness.
Instead, marriage often reveals how much selfishness still remains.
It is an invitation for sanctification.
The Holy Spirit often uses marriage as one of His greatest classrooms.
There is another truth our culture desperately needs to hear.
No human being can carry the weight of being your savior.
That burden belongs to Christ alone.
When we expect a spouse to heal every wound...
We ask them to carry a cross only Jesus could bear.
Eventually they collapse beneath expectations God never gave them.
Only Christ satisfies the deepest hunger of the human heart.
"Whoever comes to me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst." (John 6:35)
Never confuse the gift with the Savior.
Perhaps you carry shame from a broken relationship.
Perhaps you've made decisions you wish you could erase.
Perhaps your story feels too damaged.
The Gospel was written for stories exactly like yours.
The Greek word μετάνοια (metánoia), commonly translated "repentance," literally describes a transformed mind leading to a transformed life.
Repentance is not merely feeling guilty.
Because of Him, your past no longer has the final word.
That is why our heartbeat remains:
The Samaritan woman had multiple broken relationships.
Yet God's grace rewrote every one of their stories.
If you are waiting for marriage...
Become the person you are praying to find.
A healthy marriage is rarely built by two people desperately searching for each other.
It is more often built by two people who were already wholeheartedly seeking Christ.
Your identity is beloved child of God through faith in Jesus Christ.
That truth cannot be taken away.
If this message challenged you, don't let it end here.
What spoke to your heart the most?
Your testimony may become the encouragement another believer has been praying for today.
One faithful act of sharing can place biblical truth into a heart exactly when God intends it.
One surrendered heart can become the beginning of generations transformed by the Gospel.
